title: Windows Firewall profile disable command
description: Detects Netsh or PowerShell commands requesting Windows Firewall profile disablement. The false value must be the Enabled argument; process start alone does not establish a changed firewall state.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may disable Windows Firewall profiles to remove host-level network restrictions before remote access, command and control, or lateral movement.
hypothesis.rationale: Microsoft recommends keeping Windows Firewall enabled and documents the exact Netsh and PowerShell disable commands, while MITRE identifies disabling Windows host-firewall profiles as defense impairment.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify Netsh and PowerShell commands that set Windows Firewall profile state to disabled while leaving profile enablement and ordinary firewall-rule administration unmatched.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint process events

triage.summary: Determine which firewall profiles were disabled, who initiated the change and whether the endpoint became newly reachable or initiated unusual traffic.
steps: Confirm the command's result in follow-on process, file, registry or service telemetry; a process-start event records intent and does not prove successful execution.
Review the command line, account, elevation, parent process, endpoint role and affected firewall profiles.
Confirm an approved troubleshooting, security-tool deployment or policy-maintenance change and inspect the effective firewall state.
Correlate with remote access, listening services and subsequent network connections; restore policy and contain unexplained activity.
false_positives: Approved troubleshooting, security-product installation and controlled firewall-policy maintenance

validation.expected_outcome: Match Netsh or PowerShell commands that disable Windows Firewall profiles; do not match profile enablement, normal rule creation or another binary.

limitations: The recorded configuration event does not establish malicious intent, persistence effectiveness or the final security state. Verify the actor, value, approval and subsequent behavior.
Current-revision evidence is synthetic only. Validate full generated KQL, source fields, ingestion delay, alert volume and scoped exclusions in the target before enabling.
